paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim, at the beginning of chapter 4: R' Yaakov bar Acha; R' Shimon Bolota in the name of R' Chanina.
In Taanit 4:2, Hyman says R' Bolata appears in error and should read R' Shimon Bolota; see the entry Belavta.

notes.text: Hyman lists Yaakov bar Acha and Shimon Bolota without a connector. His Taanit correction supplies Shimon in place of the bare Bolata form.

The saved whole Mechon-Mamre JerusalemTalmudPesachim4:1 scalar explicitly has Yaakov bar Acha, Shimon Bolota, in Chanina’s name. It supports beginning of chapter4 rather than the old end reading. These exact titles are abbreviated ר׳, so R' is retained without a global Rabbi expansion. Taanit4:2 and Hyman’s claimed Bolata-to-Shimon-Bolota correction were not newly inspected; the latter remains his assertion. Belavta remains the separate supplied cross-reference spelling. No name identity or source-hold clearance follows.

In Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:2:5, Mechon-Mamre has the bare name R’ Bolata, while the Venice and Guggenheimer texts name R’ Shimon as בולווטה and בּוּלֶוְוטָה respectively. The passage concerns the song accompanying the Temple offering, as does the cited Pesachim passage. Hyman’s proposed replacement is retained, and Belavta remains his separate cross-reference.
